doubtful: the citation is 'l. Quod ſi nolit § Qui mancipia', whose title is D. de ædilicio edicto, so these two lines should give 'D. de' / 'ædil. edic.'. Measured at 8x (margin-1.jpg y799-906) the print will not support it: the two letters after 'D.' are both x-height (no ascender, so not 'de'), widths 26 and 21 px = a + e; and the next line opens a(26) d(27, ascender) i(15) l(7) = 'adil.', not 'ædil.'. Transcribed as the glyphs stand; 'ae' here may be the æ sort (3 px gap) and the line pair may be a compositor's error. Worth a re-check at high zoom

abbreviations in small italic, read with difficulty: 'ſtio' completes 'quæſtio' from the line above; the single letter before 'ſi' is read as c (chapitre) with its point, and the last word as 'gena.'. A tick sits above the end of the word which may be a tilde or an i-dot. The whole citation reads 'l. ſuper ſtatu. C. de quæſtio. c. ſi gena. en la diſtinction lvj.'
